meta.title: Illustrative HFACS: late touchdown on a wet runway
meta.scope: Invented teaching example, not a real event. Follows the four levels and 17 categories of Shappell & Wiegmann (2000), DOT/FAA/AM-00/7. Evidence fields say "invented" on purpose.

event.text: A turboprop touches down long on a wet runway and stops beyond the runway end (invented example)

factors.text: Recurrent training hours for wet-runway landings were reduced to cut cost.
The operator’s procedures had no stabilised-approach criteria and no mandatory go-around call.
Line checks did not observe how crews calculated landing distance.
Repeated long-landing reports from the same base were filed but not acted on.
The crew was focused on making the scheduled gate time.
The co-pilot’s call about excess speed was not acknowledged; go-around criteria were not briefed.
The landing was continued from an unstabilised approach.
Brakes were applied late after touchdown.
